title: The ordinary-double-point gap in every dimension
main_claim: For n>=2, every singular boundary-zero klt n-dimensional germ has normalized volume at most 2(n-1)^n, with equality exactly at an analytic ordinary double point. The proof is by induction from dimensions 2, 3 and 4, with dimension 4 taken from the fourfold companion paper.

issues.location: Sec. 3, Li–Zhou input (Prop 2.6 of arXiv:2502.11847v1), used before eq. (small:primitive-curve-degree)
issues.description: The small-stabilizer case depends on an external existence result taken as cited: an orbifold rational curve P(1,l)->B, with at most one stack point, whose anticanonical degree plus inverse age is at most dim B+1. Only the weaker bound re/l <= n is used. I could not check this against the cited preprint.
issues.evidence: 'In this setting it supplies a representable nonconstant map from P(1,l) ... whose anticanonical degree plus the inverse age at that point is at most dim B+1.'

issues.location: Sec. 2 (Theorem inp:fourfold) and the external inputs CS19, XZ21/XZStable, LWX21, BL21
issues.description: Correctness depends on the fourfold companion's Theorem 1.1, used as the base case. Sibling audits at rank 206 found no gap in it. It also depends on standard but deep cited results: the Fano-cone YTD theorem, stable degeneration, uniqueness of minimizers and lower semicontinuity. These are used within their stated hypotheses as far as I can tell.
issues.evidence: Sole companion input is [FourfoldCompanion, Thm 1.1]; the Ricci-flat cone metric comes from [CS19, Thm 1.1].

sibling_notes: Family 037: three earlier passes on the fourfold companion (rank 206) all reported no_gap_found. That paper is the sole companion input here (Theorem inp:fourfold, used as the n=4 base case). I found no circular dependence: this paper uses only the companion's statement, and the dimension-n step uses only the definition of M_n, not a bound on it.
